blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At the top of an organisation, the scarcest resource is not money. It is the collective attention of the leadership team — and, more precisely, the attention of the small group whose permission and energy are required for any real change to happen. Strategic leaders protect that attention the way investors protect capital, because it is, structurally, the same kind of thing.

Most organisations say they are focused, and very few actually are. Focus reveals itself in subtraction: the projects you stopped, the meetings you declined, the opportunities you deliberately let pass. A company with twelve strategic priorities has, in practice, none. Narrowing the list is painful, political and often personal — which is precisely why so few teams do it properly.

Having decided what matters, the next question is how to protect that decision from quiet erosion. New requests arrive every week, each sensible in isolation; over months, they quietly repopulate the calendar, re-fill the agenda and restore the previous chaos. Strategic discipline is, very largely, the discipline of saying a polite, specific and consistent no.

items.q: According to the text, what is the scarcest resource at the top of an organisation?
options: Time before the next reporting cycle
Skilled operational staff
The leadership team's collective attention
Capital
items.why: "the scarcest resource is not money. It is the collective attention of the leadership team."

items.q: The text says that focus "reveals itself in subtraction." This means focus is shown by…
options: the size of the leadership team
what a company deliberately stops or declines
the number of initiatives a company launches
how quickly new requests are approved
items.why: "the projects you stopped, the meetings you declined, the opportunities you deliberately let pass."

items.q: Why does the author say a company with twelve strategic priorities has "in practice, none"?
options: Because twelve is too few to be strategic
Because so many priorities mean nothing is truly prioritised
Because the priorities were chosen politically
Because priorities should always be set by one person
items.why: Inferência: prioridade demais equivale a nenhuma — nada recebe atenção diferenciada.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Approving every sensible request keeps a team strategically focused.
Once priorities are set, they tend to erode quietly over time.
Saying no is central to strategic discipline.
Each new request, taken alone, can look perfectly reasonable.
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta o oposto — aceitar todo pedido razoável é justamente o que corrói o foco.

items.q: What does the phrase "quiet erosion" suggest about how focus is lost?
options: It is lost gradually and almost unnoticed, request by request
It is lost when budgets are cut
It is lost suddenly, through one big decision
It is lost only when leaders change
items.why: Inferência: "quietly repopulate the calendar… restore the previous chaos" — a perda é lenta e imperceptível.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily orientando o comitê executivo. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, let's be honest with each other. We came into this room with twelve strategic priorities, and I've heard everyone defend their own with real conviction. But conviction isn't the test here. The test is subtraction.

Having listened all morning, I think the four that survive are fairly clear — and I can see that two of you are uncomfortable, because your programmes aren't on that list. I want to name that directly rather than pretend it isn't happening. Deprioritising something you've built is genuinely hard, and it isn't a judgement on the work.

Here's my concern. Even if we agree the four today, the calendar will fight back. Next quarter, sensible requests will arrive one by one, each easy to say yes to, and by the summer we'll quietly be running twelve again. So the decision we make this afternoon isn't really about the list. It's about whether we can hold the line afterwards — a polite, specific, consistent no, week after week.

Attention is our capital. Let's spend it like people who know it's finite.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: According to Emily, what is the real "test" for a strategic priority?
options: Whether the whole committee likes it
Whether it can be subtracted, not just defended
How strongly its sponsor defends it
How much revenue it is expected to generate
items.why: "conviction isn't the test here. The test is subtraction."

items.q: Why does Emily say two committee members are uncomfortable?
options: They disagree with the whole exercise
They were not consulted in advance
They want more than four priorities
Their programmes are not among the four that survive
items.why: "two of you are uncomfortable, because your programmes aren't on that list."

items.q: What does Emily mean when she says "the calendar will fight back"?
options: New requests will gradually undo the decision over the coming months
The board will reject the four priorities
The scheduling software will need to be reconfigured
The team will run out of meeting slots
items.why: Inferência: pedidos razoáveis chegam um a um e, sem disciplina, o comitê volta às doze prioridades.

items.q: According to Emily, the decision made this afternoon is really about…
options: who should sponsor each priority
whether the team can hold the line and keep saying no afterwards
which four priorities to choose
how to communicate the list to the board
items.why: "It's about whether we can hold the line afterwards — a polite, specific, consistent no."

items.q: How would you best describe Emily's approach with the two uncomfortable sponsors?
options: She ignores their discomfort to keep the meeting moving
She acknowledges it directly while making clear it isn't a judgement on their work
She lets them keep their programmes to avoid conflict
She blames them for the loss of focus
items.why: Inferência: ela nomeia o desconforto abertamente e separa a despriorização da qualidade do trabalho.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We treat attention as capital — finite, and spent whether we notice or not." This framing means attention is…
options: an unlimited resource that costs nothing
something only investors care about
a scarce resource to be allocated deliberately, like money
a purely emotional state
items.why: Attention as capital = atenção como capital: recurso finito que se aloca com critério.

items.q: "Choosing to fund this launch means declining that acquisition; the opportunity cost is real." Opportunity cost is…
options: the risk that the project fails
a hidden tax on new projects
the cash spent on the chosen option
the value of the best alternative you gave up
items.why: Opportunity cost = custo de oportunidade: o valor da melhor alternativa abandonada.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Every quarter, unlogged side-projects form a ___ that no one has formally agreed to."
options: leadership bandwidth
hidden backlog
strategic priority
quiet erosion
items.why: Hidden backlog = backlog oculto: trabalho acumulado que ninguém aprovou formalmente.

items.q: "We simply don't have the leadership bandwidth to sponsor all twelve." Leadership bandwidth is…
options: the number of layers in the hierarchy
the leadership team's budget
the speed of the internal network
the finite time and attention senior leaders can devote
items.why: Leadership bandwidth = capacidade de liderança: o tempo e a atenção finitos dos líderes seniores.

items.q: Choose the correct verb: "If we don't formally ___ two of these, they'll keep drawing on the same scarce attention."
options: repopulate
deprioritise
narrow
erode
items.why: To deprioritise = despriorizar: rebaixar deliberadamente algo para liberar atenção.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre foco e prioridades. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The committee has to hold the line once the four priorities are set." To hold the line means to…
options: wait on the phone
maintain a position and not give way under pressure
draw a new org chart
escalate the decision upwards
items.why: Hold the line = manter a posição, não ceder diante da pressão.

items.q: "Two sponsors pushed back on the cull of their programmes." They…
options: rewrote it themselves
resisted or challenged the decision
forgot about it
approved it at once
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "None of these small requests will move the needle on our strategy." This means they will…
options: make no noticeable difference
arrive too late to matter
cost more than expected
provoke resistance
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "Let's weed out anything that doesn't serve the four priorities." To weed out means to…
options: combine into one programme
delegate to another team
postpone indefinitely
remove what is unwanted or unhelpful
items.why: Weed out = eliminar o que não serve, tirar o supérfluo.

items.q: "We agreed the list, but nobody followed through on stopping the old projects." They…
options: reopened the debate
carried the decision to completion
failed to see the decision through to the end
documented it in detail
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui, o oposto aconteceu.
